name: RDP Brute Force (multiple failed Windows logons from one source)
triage: 8+ failed Windows logons (EventID 4625, network/RDP logon type) from one source IP within 2 minutes. Investigate the source, confirm no successful 4624 followed, and consider account lockout / NLA enforcement.

name: New local account added to Administrators
triage: A local account was created (EventID 4720) and shortly after added to the Administrators group (EventID 4732) on the same host. Confirm this change was authorized; attackers create admin accounts for persistence and privilege.

name: Suspicious PowerShell encoded command
triage: PowerShell launched with an -EncodedCommand / -enc argument. Attackers use base64-encoded commands to hide intent. Decode the command, review the parent process, and confirm whether it was an approved admin/automation action.

name: Scheduled task created
triage: A scheduled task was created (Security EventID 4698 or schtasks.exe execution). Scheduled tasks are a common persistence mechanism. Verify the task name, the action it runs, and the user that created it against change records.

name: Scheduled task created

name: Windows Security event log cleared
triage: The Windows Security audit log was cleared (EventID 1102). This is a classic anti-forensics / defense-evasion action. Correlate with the account that performed it and any activity immediately preceding the clear.

name: Port scan from a single source (many distinct destination ports)
triage: A single source IP contacted 15+ distinct destination ports within 60 seconds (network connection EventID 3). This pattern indicates host/port scanning or service discovery. Identify the source and whether it is an authorized scanner.

name: Microsoft Defender real-time protection disabled
triage: A command disabled Microsoft Defender real-time monitoring (Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true). This is defense evasion and should almost never happen outside maintenance windows. Re-enable protection and investigate the account/host immediately.

name: Web shell-like request in web access logs
triage: A request targeting a PHP endpoint with command-execution style parameters (cmd=, whoami, /uploads/...). Possible web shell interaction. Inspect the web root for unauthorized .php files, review the source IP's full request history, and check server-side process execution.

name: Office application spawning a command shell
triage: A Microsoft Office application (Word/Excel/...) spawned a command interpreter (cmd/powershell/...). This is a hallmark of malicious document execution (user opened a weaponized attachment). Isolate the host, capture the parent document, and review what the child process did.
